items.headline: Chip and AI-infrastructure stocks sell off after Democrats win both chambers of Congress
items.why: Markets are pricing a higher chance of AI regulation and data-center limits, and they are splitting spenders (Amazon and Microsoft rose over 6% on Nov 4) from suppliers (Micron, CoreWeave and Marvell fell sharply).

items.headline: Qualcomm falls more than 11% as handset-chip sales drop 26% to $5.1 billion
items.why: Smartphone weakness plus Apple's shift to its own modems removes the company's core growth leg, so its pivot to auto, industrial and data-center revenue now has to carry the story.

items.headline: Apple guides holiday-quarter gross margin down to 45-46% on rising memory prices; AMD forecasts 80% sales growth in 2027
items.why: Memory-chip inflation is now squeezing hardware makers while data-center demand lifts chip designers, a split that determines who captures the AI build-out's profits.

items.headline: October US CPI rises 0.4% against 0.3% expected; core holds at 0.3% for a third straight month
items.why: Sticky shelter and services inflation shows the energy-driven spike has not been the only source of price pressure, which keeps the Fed on a tightening path.

items.headline: Markets price a December Fed hike as near-certain and about 54% odds of another in January
items.why: The 2-year yield jumped 14 basis points to 4.69% on the print, so tightening is now the base case that equities and credit have to absorb.

items.why: Long yields above 5% on the 30-year raise discount rates on expensive tech valuations and tighten financial conditions beyond what the Fed itself does.
